title: Processing does not lengthen the remaining path
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\mathit{lits}$ be a list of literals on $n$ variables each tagged with its position index, let $\mathit{path}$ be a list of decision-tree branch entries (each a variable together with a Boolean direction), and let $\rho_0, \sigma$ be restrictions on $n$ variables. Then the remaining path returned by processing $\mathit{lits}$ against $\mathit{path}$ starting from $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$ — that is, the first component of the result of this processing — has length at most the length of $\mathit{path}$.
hypotheses_covered: a list of literals with position indices on n variables
a decision-tree path (list of variable/direction entries)
two restrictions ρ₀ and σ on n variables
replaced:
The remaining path returned by \texttt{processClauseLits} is no longer than the input
path: the length of the first component of $\mathrm{processClauseLits}\,(\mathit{lits},
\mathit{path}, \rho_0, \sigma)$ is at most the length of $\mathit{path}$.
